messages:
maya: Heads-up — customer reported duplicate token charges when a client reconnects after network flaps. They see two inflight resume flows for the same logical session.
jon: Ugh. Is this the opaque session id we switched to? Any logs? :eyes:
maya: Logs show two separate connections with different connection IDs but same resume_token in payload. Billing meter keyed by connection_id so both increment.
leo: So billing uses connection_id rather than resume_token/session_id? That sounds like a mismatch between router and billing pipeline.
tara: Right — router currently binds quotas to the per-connection session object for simpler eviction. Resume_token was only used for KV cache restore, not quota dedupe.
jon: That explains it. Quick question: are these reconnects both routed to different backends? If yes, we might also be double-counting because sticky routing isn't enforced on resume.
maya: In the incident traces most resumed connections hit different pods due to sticky timeout. There was a region failover too.
leo: We should add resume_token as a tag on quota-metering events so billing can dedupe within a short window. Also add session_id to telemetry to correlate.
tara: Agreed. Propose change: meter keys = [customer_id, resume_token||connection_id] for first 60s post-connect, then fallback to connection_id. That way resume within a minute is deduped. Thoughts?
jon: Seems reasonable. Need to be careful with privacy — resume_token is internal, but we already log it in traces. Make sure it's hashed before sending to billing pipeline.
maya: Good call. Hashing acceptable. Also console/dashboard UX: current per-route dashboard shows spikes but can't tell they were reconnections. We should surface a "session continuity" line in the per-route latency/cost graph (count resumed vs new sessions).
leo: Implementation plan: 1) router emits metric counter `connections.start` with label `session_hash` and `resumed=true/false` 2) billing consumer dedupes by session_hash for 60s 3) console adds stacked series for resumed/new connections.
jon: For rollout, feature flag guarded, canary to 5% of traffic, and a canary-only metrics pipeline to validate dedupe behavior. Also add an alert if dedupe delta > 1% of normal billing delta.
maya: I sketched quick SSE reconnect example for client docs:
```
# client reconnect example
GET /v1/stream?model=gpt-embed
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer $KEY
  X-Resume-Token: abc123def456
# on reconnect, include same X-Resume-Token header
```
jon: Nice. One more: telemetry gap — our current traces don't include the original connection_id when resume happens, so console's trace view can't join events. We should emit an `origin_connection_id` on resume events.
tara: Can we avoid PII? Both connection ids are internal ephemeral strings, fine if kept internal and redacted in public exports.
leo: I'll open PR for router change (emit hashed session tag + origin_connection_id on resume). jon can add billing consumer dedupe. maya can own console UX bits and docs.
jon: I'll also add unit tests for corner cases: two resumes with different resume_tokens but same customer_id (no dedupe), same resume_token but >60s apart (no dedupe).
maya: SRE bot pinged: sre-bot: incident created: INC-9872 for customer billing spike. deploy-bot: deploy queued for canary feature-flag branch.
leo: Timeline — aim to have router PR by EOD tomorrow, billing consumer PR in 3 days, console patch next week.
tara: Also add a metric to measure "resume_meter_mismatch" so we can detect older clients that don't send X-Resume-Token.
jon: Sounds good. Thanks all. I'll draft the RFC and link it here. :thumbsup:
